newsitem.title: UK: S&P rates Greece's Municipality of Amaroussion.
newsitem.headline: S&P rates Greece's Municipality of Amaroussion.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Monday it had assigned its BB plus local and foreign currency long-term issuer credit rating to the Municipality of Amaroussion.
"The outlook is stable," S&P said in a statement.
The Municipality of Amaroussion is located in the metropolitan area of the Greek capital Athens.
S&P said the rating took account of the following factors.
- The city's favourable location within the least developed country in the European Union.
- Its service based economy with income levels above the national average.
- The unstructured relationship between the central government and municpalities, with expected declines in central government transfers likely to put pressure on municipal finances going forward.
- The municipality's large and stable operating balances and modest debt burden.
- The poor liquidity and financial flexibility given the narrow access of Greek municipalities to the domestic capital markets.
With 90,000 inhabitants in 1996, Amaroussion is the 15th largest Greek municipality in terms of population, S&P said.

"Over the last few years, the city has consolidated and is now one of Athens' main business and employment centres," the rating agency said. "About 60,000 people commute into the city every working day. The city's adequate level of basic infrastructure and its good transport links with central Athens have made it a very attractive business location and some of the largest national and multinational companies have established their headquarters there."
S&P said Amaroussion's economic structure was largely concentrated on service activities, which accounted for 70 percent of total employment.

"Although there is no detailed data on the city's income levels, Amaroussion's officials estimate that per capita income in the municipality is very similar to the average in Athens, which is 20 percent above the national level," S&P said.
"Economic growth prospects look good in light of the city's rapidly increasing population, good location and position as a business centre."
S&P said Amaroussion's operating balances had traditionally been very high, ranging between 35 and 57 percent of operating revenues over the last five years.

"Further debt accumulation will occur in coming years as the municipality completes its ongoing investment programme," the agency said. "According to local officials, debt should peak at a maximum of 100 percent of operating revenues in the year 2000."

"The city's financial flexibility and liquidity are poor since the country's financial markets are reluctant to lend funds to municipalities. Cash holdings are low and no credit lines are available for the municipality."
S&P said although direct debt was expected to increase to fund the region's ambitious investment programme, overall debt levels would continue to be manageable.
"The city's location and its position as a main business centre should boost economic prospects going forward," S&P said.
